title: Assembly of Cell Mimicking Supported and Suspended Lipid Bilayer Models for the Study of Molecular Interactions
protocol: Prepare a 10 mg/mL lipid stock solution by adding the appropriate volume of chloroform into the vial containing the lipid powder and mix well.
Transfer the lipid stock solution to a glass vial with a PTFE-lined cap if stored in an ampule.
Seal the vial cap with Parafilm and store at -20 °C for up to 6 months.
Add the appropriate volume of lipid stock solution into a clean glass vial needed for a final vesicle concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Remove chloroform from lipid stock solution using a stream of N2 gas (ultrapure 5.0 Grade).
Connect the dried lipid film to vacuum and leave for at least 4 hours.
Rehydrate the dried lipid film with Tris sodium chloride buffer to yield a final vesicle concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Vortex the rehydrated lipid suspension for approximately 15-30 seconds.
Transfer the vesicle suspension into a container with dry ice until frozen, approximately 30 minutes.
Thaw the frozen vesicle suspension in a 30-40 °C water bath.
Vortex the thawed vesicle suspension.
Repeat freeze-thaw-vortex cycles an additional 4 times for a total of 5 cycles.
Extrude the vesicles using a mini (1 mL) extruder to form large unilamellar vesicles.
Thoroughly clean all components of the extruder using a mild detergent in ultrapure water.
Rinse at least three times with ultrapure water to ensure all detergent is removed.
Dry with N2 gas.
Assemble two internal membrane supports and O-rings (inner diameter of 12.7 mm; outer diameter of 15.2 mm).
Position each membrane support so the O-ring faces up.
Pre-wet a filter support with ultrapure water.
Place it on the membrane support surface inside the O-ring.
Repeat for the second internal membrane support.
Position one internal membrane support into the extruder outer casing.
Place one 100 nm polycarbonate membrane onto the internal membrane support, directly over the filter support.
Remove separating paper before inserting the polycarbonate membrane.
Position the second internal membrane support into the extruder outer casing with the O-ring and filter support facing the first membrane.
Attach the PTFE bearing into the retainer nut and screw closed with the extruder outer casing.
Clip the extruder into the heating block.
Load the lipid vesicle suspension into one syringe.
Position the filled syringe into the extruder heat block, inserting the needle fully into one end of the extruder.
Insert the second empty syringe into the opposite side of the extruder.
Lock both syringes using the arm clips on the heat block.
If heat is required, place the extruder heat block on a hot plate and set the temperature above the lipid transition temperature.
Insert a thermometer into the holder built into the heat block for accurate temperature readings.
Wait until the required temperature is reached (~15 min).
Slowly push the vesicle suspension into the empty syringe and then back into the original syringe.
Monitor for pressure changes throughout the extrusion to indicate leaks.
Repeat 20 more times for a total of 21 passes through the polycarbonate membrane.
Transfer the lipid vesicles into a clean glass vial for storage.
Fill a 1 L flask with reverse osmosis (RO) water.
Place the 1 L flask in a water bath on a hot plate.
Set the hot plate temperature above the lipid transition temperature.
Attach the sample cylinder inlet to the flask using flexible tubing.
Connect tubing from the outlet of the cylinder to the top of the 1 L flask.
Secure tubing at both the inlet and outlet.
Turn on the pump to start water circulation.
Allow approximately 30-45 minutes for the sample cylinder to reach desired temperature if heat is needed.
Clean all parts of the 50 mL extruder with 70% (v/v) ethanol.
Place the large hole screen support into the space in the extruder lower support.
Insert a sintered disk into the space.
Add drain disks into the space.
Install a polycarbonate membrane into the space.
Connect the extruder upper and lower supports using four screws.
Tighten the connection between the extruder upper and lower supports.
Attach the extruder unit to the sample cylinder by screwing it to the bottom.
Secure the extruder unit with a wrench.
Place a thermometer into the cylinder and wait until water has reached desired temperature before continuing.
Fill the sample cylinder with ultrapure water.
Extrude the water through the extruder unit prior to adding the sample into the sample cylinder.
Ensure the cap is fully screwed on and the pressure relief valve is closed completely before turning on the nitrogen.
Add the lipid vesicle suspension into the sample cylinder and screw the top closed.
Slowly increase the pressure until the sample begins to drip from the extruder unit at a rate of approximately 2-3 drops/s into a clean glass vial.
Pour the lipid vesicles back into the sample cylinder.
Repeat the extrusion process 9 more times for a total of 10 extrusions.
Store extruded lipid vesicle suspension at 4 °C.
Vortex lipid vesicles.
Pipette 50 µL of the lipid vesicle suspension into a disposable low-volume cuvette.
Cover the cuvette to prevent contamination with dust and debris.
Load the vesicle suspension into the DLS instrument.
Input the sample details in the associated software.
Perform the measurement using the associated software.
Prepare a folded capillary zeta cell by washing with ultrapure water, 70% ethanol, and ultrapure water using syringes that connect to the inputs of the cell.
Gently push the liquid through the cell 3-4 times.
Empty the cell completely before switching to the next solution.
Vortex the lipid vesicles.
Prepare a 1:10 (v/v) dilution of lipid vesicles in ultrapure water.
Load the diluted lipid vesicle suspension into the zeta cell.
Remove air bubbles by pushing the suspension back and forth between the syringes.
Attach stoppers to each inlet of the zeta cell.
Place the zeta cell in the sample chamber, ensuring that the electrodes are in contact.
Close the sample chamber top.
Input the sample details in the associated software.
Collect measurement using the associated software.
Prepare a 2% (w/v) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) solution in ultrapure water.
Mix on a stir plate until completely dissolved.
Aliquot working solutions of at least 10 mL of ultrapure water, 2% SDS, and Tris NaCl.
Dilute lipid vesicles in Tris NaCl buffer as needed for the application.
Insert the silica-coated quartz crystal sensor into the flow module ensuring proper alignment.
Screw the flow module closed.
Connect the flow module to the base of the instrument with electrodes properly connected.
Lock the module into place.
Connect the inlet and outlet tubing to the flow module and pump.
Place the tubing into the holding guards and close the lid of the analyzer system.
Place a waste container at the outlet of the pump to collect spent solutions.
Turn on the pump.
Set the flow speed to 400 μL/min.
Insert the inlet tubing into ultrapure water and flow 5-10 mL through the module.
Switch the inlet tubing into 2% SDS and flow 5-10 mL through the module.
Switch the inlet tubing back into ultrapure water and flow 10-20 mL through the module.
Remove the inlet tubing from the solution and flow air through the tubing until all liquid is ejected.
Insert the silica-coated quartz crystal sensor into the UV/ozone cleaning instrument.
Turn on the UV/ozone cleaning instrument and treat for at least 2 min.
Remove the treated sensors carefully and return them to the flow module.
Turn on the analyzer instrument and connect to the associated software.
Set the temperature of the analyzer to the desired value for the supported lipid bilayer.
Allow the temperature to stabilize.
Heat all solutions to the set temperature using a heat block if necessary.
Configure the measurement and find resonance frequencies and dissipations for overtones 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 13.
Turn on the pump and set the flow rate to 175 μL/min or desired experimental flow rate.
Wipe the inlet tubing with ethanol prior to insertion into Tris NaCl.
Start the measurement and begin flowing Tris NaCl through the module.
Allow Tris NaCl to flow for 5-10 min, ensuring baseline ΔF and ΔD values remain stable.
Stop the pump and remove the inlet tubing from the Tris NaCl solution.
Insert the inlet tubing into the lipid vesicle solution carefully.
Back flow for 5 s to remove air bubbles from the inlet tubing.
Continue forward flow after removing air bubbles.
Restart measurement in software to zero baseline.
Flow lipid vesicles until bilayer formation is observed in real-time data acquisition software (at least 8 min for egg PC vesicles).
Change inlet tubing from lipid vesicles back into Tris NaCl buffer.
Stop measurement and save file if bilayer formation is endpoint.
Clean the flow module and silica-coated quartz crystal sensor following protocol steps.
Add 5 μL of lipid solution to the donor compartment on a PVDF 96-well multiscreen filter plate.
Submerge the filter plate into an acceptor compartment containing 300 μL of 1× phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Add 200 μL of 1× PBS to the donor compartment.
Culture the desired cell line until it reaches 70-80% confluence in a T75 flask.
Detach cells using trypsin-ethylenediaminetretaacetic acid at 37 °C for 5 min.
Centrifuge cells at 200 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of ultrapure water.
Add 3.75 mL of a 1:2 (v/v) mixture of chloroform:methanol to the cell suspension and vortex for 15 min.
Add 1.25 mL of chloroform and vortex for 1 min.
Add 1.25 mL of water and vortex for 1 min.
Centrifuge the cell mixture at 1000 x g for 10 min.
Collect the bottom layer containing lipids in the organic phase.
Dry the collected lipid layer under a stream of N2 gas.
Prepare two mobile phase solutions: the first with 60:40 (v/v) acetonitrile:water and the second with 90:10 (v/v) isopropanol:acetonitrile.
Add ammonium formate to both mobile phase solutions at a final concentration of 10 mM.
Increase the mobile phase gradient from 35% (v/v) of the second solution to 95% (v/v) over 60 min.
Detect the effluent in negative ionization mode, with consecutive full-scan MS and tandem MS/MS.
Identify individual phospholipid species from their mass-to-charge (m/z) ratios.
Analyze the mass spectra from collision-induced dissociation fragmentation using LIPID MAPS mass spectrometry analysis tools.
Obtain extracted ion chromatograms to integrate the area under the curve, determining the abundance of each lipid species.
Quantify the relative sensitivity of detection for each different phospholipid class based on a lipid standard containing major lipid classes.
Prepare lipid stock solutions for lipids representing each desired bilayer component as identified in step 5.1.
Add appropriate volume of lipid/chloroform stock into a clean glass vial to achieve a final vesicle concentration of 2.5 mg/mL.
Remove bulk chloroform drying solution under a stream of N2 gas.
Follow steps 1.1.2, 1.1.3, and 1.2 to form multi-lipid vesicles.
Follow step 2 for vesicle characterization.
Form a multi-lipid supported lipid bilayer using QCM-D.
Prepare the AH peptide solution at 13 μM in Tris NaCl with 1% (v/v) dimethylsulfoxide, DMSO.
Change the inlet tubing into the AH peptide solution after step 3.4.3.
Introduce the AH peptide solution into the flow module until ΔF and ΔD are observed from the new solution addition.
Stop the pump and allow the AH peptide to incubate with the vesicles for 10 minutes.
Switch the inlet tubing into Tris NaCl.
Start the flow to remove the AH peptide from the ruptured vesicles leading to successful formation of a lipid bilayer.
Continue direction to step 6.1 without stopping the solution flow or data acquisition if studying molecular interactions is desired.
Stop the measurement and save the file in the software.
Stop the pump.
Clean the flow module following protocol steps 3.2.4-3.2.6.
Solubilize mixture of desired lipids in dodecane at 20 mg/mL.
Make up a 5 μL lipid mix solution using the desired cell mimicking composition.
Follow steps 4.2 and 4.3 for suspended multi-lipid bilayers.
Continue directly to step 6.2 to investigate molecular interactions with the suspended lipid bilayer.
Prepare a solution of the desired molecule to investigate adsorption with a supported lipid bilayer.
For example, prepare a solution of 200 μM di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) in Tris NaCl with 1% (v/v) DMSO.
If the molecule solution is prepared in Tris NaCl, it can be flowed directly following step 3.4.3 for a uni-lipid bilayer or 5.3.4 for a multi-lipid bilayer.
If the molecule must be prepared in a different solvent, instead insert the inlet tubing into the desired solvent alone for at least 5 min (e.g., Tris NaCl with 1% (v/v) DMSO for DEHP).
Switch the inlet tubing into the solution containing the molecule of interest and flow for at least 5 min.
The flow may also be stopped and liquid containing the desired molecule allowed to incubate with the bilayer if desired.
Change the inlet tubing back to the molecule solvent alone if something other than Tris NaCl.
Flow for at least 5 min.
Then, switch the inlet tubing into Tris NaCl and flow for at least 5 min.
In the software, stop the measurement and save the file.
Stop the pump.
Clean the flow module and silica-coated quartz crystal sensor following the protocol steps 3.2.4-3.2.6.
Prepare a new transport receiver plate with 300 μL of fresh 1x PBS per well.
Remove 1× PBS from the donor compartment of the multiscreen filter plate.
Replace with 200 μL of the test solution in the donor compartment.
Submerge the multiscreen filter plate in the transport receiver plate.
Incubate with gentle rocking for a desired amount of time (e.g., 2 h) at 25 °C.
Collect 150 μL of the solution from the donor and acceptor compartments after incubation.
Measure the molecule concentration in both samples using an appropriate method based on properties of this molecule.
Calculate the apparent permeability (Papp) of the molecule of interest using the provided equations.
